<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תמוז_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518919223_theRebbe_96" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_9E_D7_95_D7_96_meluket__BH_POST_1766518919223_theRebbe_96__p009">
  <section v="24">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the beginning of the psalm speaks of Malchus as it ascends in its root in Atik, while the end of the psalm speaks of Atik drawn down into Malchus and then into the lower worlds, ultimately for Israel and the future redemption.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And it must be said that this is that the beginning of the psalm is “Ad-noy, You have been a dwelling place,” etc.,</t>
    <t s="1">and the end of the psalm is “And may the pleasantness of Ad-noy, our Lord, be upon us,” etc.,</t>
    <t s="2">for at the beginning of the psalm it speaks about the matter of Malchus as it ascends in its root in Atik,</t>
    <t s="3">and therefore it says “dwelling place,” which refers to Malchus</t>
    <t s="4">(as above, section 2),</t>
    <t s="5">except that “dwelling place” (maon) is the letters of “pleasantness” (noam), which indicates the ascent of Malchus into Atik,</t>
    <t s="6">and at the end of the psalm it speaks about the matter of Atik</t>
    <t s="7">(“pleasantness”),</t>
    <t s="8">which is drawn down into Malchus,</t>
    <t s="9">and through Malchus—into the worlds of Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah, down to this physical world.</t>
    <t s="10">And it says, “And may the pleasantness of Ad-noy, our Lord, be upon us,”</t>
    <t s="11">for the main revelation is for Israel,</t>
    <t s="12">and through this a semblance of this revelation will be drawn into the entire world,</t>
    <t s="13">in the true and complete redemption through our righteous Moshiach,</t>
    <t s="14">very soon.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the beginning of the psalm speaks of Malchus as it ascends in its root in Atik, while the end of the psalm speaks of Atik drawn down into Malchus and then into the lower worlds, ultimately for Israel and the future redemption.

translations.translation: And it must be said that this is that the beginning of the psalm is “Ad-noy, You have been a dwelling place,” etc.,
and the end of the psalm is “And may the pleasantness of Ad-noy, our Lord, be upon us,” etc.,
for at the beginning of the psalm it speaks about the matter of Malchus as it ascends in its root in Atik,
and therefore it says “dwelling place,” which refers to Malchus
except that “dwelling place” (maon) is the letters of “pleasantness” (noam), which indicates the ascent of Malchus into Atik,
and at the end of the psalm it speaks about the matter of Atik
which is drawn down into Malchus,
and through Malchus—into the worlds of Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah, down to this physical world.
And it says, “And may the pleasantness of Ad-noy, our Lord, be upon us,”
for the main revelation is for Israel,
and through this a semblance of this revelation will be drawn into the entire world,
in the true and complete redemption through our righteous Moshiach,
